text: emmy: two tracks. (1) Audit Q internally, since any pair idea that inherits Q guarantees needs them to hold: I suspect the P1 LMI (ii) \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\preceq-\upsilon I\) is infeasible together with P2 (i) \(\sum_m A^n_{nm}=0\), and that the explicit payment (eq40) violates P4 (ii). Checking by hand and numerically in emmy/. (2) Pair level: P scores GDLs by forecast average nodal carbon intensity (CEF, eq 23, 26), while a Q-type mechanism prices coupling constraints at marginal shadow prices. I will test whether P spatial shifting reduces physical emissions or only reallocates CEF-attributed carbon, and what carbon signal a mechanism for strategic GDLs would have to use.

ada: read #1. emmy owns the Q audit and the average vs marginal CEF question; I will not duplicate, only cross-check with what I already derived by hand: (a) P1(ii) with P2(i) is infeasible: for \(v=(0,\mathbf 1\otimes u)\), \(v^\top\Psi v=-\sum_n u^\top(\sum_m A^n_{nm})u=0\); (b) for eq40 the symmetrised Jacobian is indefinite, not merely singular: with \(w_n=\varepsilon u,\ q_n=u\), \(v^\top Jv=N\alpha\|u\|^2(-\varepsilon^2+\varepsilon/(N-1))>0\); (c) eq40 gives \(\sum_m a^n_m=\alpha c/(N(N-1))>0\), violating P4(ii). I will verify numerically in ada/ and add an explicit IR counterexample. My own tracks: (T1) what Q needs from P when the capacity \(c\) is a forecast (budget imbalance, feasibility, sample schedule vs forecast floor); (T2) internal claims of P that any mechanism layer would inherit (the 33.86% figure, endogeneity of NCI to GDL dispatch).

emmy, audit of Q (scripts and outputs in emmy/q_lmi_check.py, emmy/q_ir_counterexample.py, *.out). (a) P1 (ii) is infeasible jointly with P2 (i), for every parameter choice. Take \(z\) with all \(x\)-components 0 and all price components equal to \(v\). Since \(\Psi_{nm}\) has price-price block \(-A^n_{nm}\), \[z^\top\Psi z=\sum_n v^\top\Big(-\sum_m A^n_{nm}\Big)v=0\] by P2 (i), so \(z^\top(\Psi+\Psi^\top)z=0>-\upsilon\|z\|^2\). Numerically for eq40 (N=4, \(\alpha=0.8\)) \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\) has eigenvalue +0.0433. Economically, the price game is invariant to a common shift of all prices; only the \(x\)-\(p\) coupling pins the level. So Proposition 1 does not apply to any Nash-implementing payment, and the uniqueness step invoked at the end of Theorem 4 has no proof (for eq40, interior price FOCs do force symmetric prices and \(\sum_n x_n=c\), so uniqueness may be recoverable by a direct KKT argument, not by Rosen). (b) eq40 violates P4 (ii): extracted coefficients give \(\sum_m a^n_m=\alpha c/(N(N-1))>0\). Summing P2 (iv) and P3 (iii) over \(n\) gives \(\sum_n\sum_m a^n_m=\sum_n(\theta^n-\zeta^n/N)c\), so P4 (ii) needs \(\theta\le\zeta/N\), but eq40 uses \(\theta=\alpha/(N-1)\), \(\zeta=\alpha\). (c) IR actually fails for eq40. At the NE, \(t_n=\lambda^{o\top}(x^o_n-c/N)\,(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2\), so an agent whose \(x^o_n\) is a large share of \(c\) can have \(U_n<0\). Counterexample: N=2, \(V_n=b_nx-\tfrac12x^2\), \(b=(10,1.1)\), \(c=1\), \(X_n=[0,2]\). Then \(x^o=(1,0)\), \(\lambda^o=9\), budget balance holds, and \(U_1=-4<0=V_1(0)\); a grid best-response search confirms \(-4\) is agent 1 best reply, so it is a NE. (d) The simulation sets \(Q_i=\lceil 0.96^{i+1}\rceil=1\) for all \(i\), which contradicts the geometric growth \(Q_i\ge C_b/\eta^{2(i+1)}\) that Theorem 4 needs; probably a typo for \(\tilde\eta^{-(i+1)}\), but as written the theory is not what was run. (e) Minor: from eq35 to eq36 the cross terms lose a factor 2. Consequence for the pair: using Q as the incentive layer for P inherits unproven uniqueness and a false IR claim.

emmy, average vs marginal carbon in P (emmy/cef_toy.py, cef_toy.out). P scores GDLs by \(J=\sum_t\sum_i \hat e_{i,t}\ell_{i,t}+\dots\) (eq 26) with \(\hat e\) a forecast of the proportional-sharing CEF intensity (eq 23, 24). The CEF rule of Kang et al. (P ref [13]) conserves carbon: \(\sum_i e_{i,t}L_{i,t}=E^{gen}_t-E^{loss}_t\). So when a spatial move of a GDL within one hour changes neither generation nor curtailment, total attributed carbon stays fixed, and a drop in the GDL term of \(J\) is carbon passed on to fixed loads. Toy check: 3-bus star feeder, grid at \(e_g=0.8\), PV 1.5 at bus 2, fixed loads 1 and 1, GDL of 0.5. No curtailment: moving the GDL from bus 1 to bus 2 cuts \(J_{GDL}\) from 0.267 to 0 (100 percent), leaves physical \(E\) at 0.800, raises fixed-load attribution from 0.533 to 0.800, and LME is (0.8, 0.8) before and after. With reverse flow blocked (curtailment), the same move cuts \(E\) from 1.2 to 0.8 and the \(J\) saving (0.4) equals the physical saving, with LME (0.8, 0) before the move. Physical impact is therefore \(\sum \mathrm{LME}\cdot\Delta\ell\), not \(\sum \hat e\cdot\Delta\ell\). P does not state whether PV/WT is curtailed or whether generator G is redispatched (sec 3.4 has no generation variables), and does not say whether the 33.86 percent (Case 2 vs 3) and "over 30 percent" figures are physical or attributed. I read Fig 8 (per-bus emissions) as attributed; unresolved. Prior work on LME for data-centre shifting: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.03379 ; strategic LME-responsive data centre can raise emissions: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20805v1 (no payment design, no average-intensity signal); distribution LME: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.07379 .

emmy, sharpened pair question (it replaces the scan connexion). The scan proposed wrapping P dispatch in Q mechanism for strategic GDLs. Taken literally, an exact mechanism would just implement P objective (26), and #4 shows that objective can be met by moving attributed carbon onto fixed loads. The question that needs both papers: treat a carbon-responsibility rule as a payment rule. Let \(\kappa_n(x)\) be the carbon charged to GDL \(n\) with load profile \(x_n\), and let physical emissions be \(E(\ell)\) with \(\ell=\sum_n x_n+\ell^{fix}\). Three properties: (C1) conservation, \(\sum_n\kappa_n+\kappa^{fix}=E\), which is the analogue of Q budget balance P3; (C2) alignment, meaning unilateral best replies to \(\kappa_n\) implement \(\max\sum_n V_n\) subject to \(E\le E^{cap}\) (analogue of Q P2); (C3) no fixed load is charged more after GDLs move (a carbon analogue of IR). CEF (P) gives C1, fails C2 and C3 (toy: fixed-load charge 0.533 to 0.800). LME pricing gives C2 but not C1, since \(\sum_i \mathrm{LME}_i L_i\ne E\) in general. Q construction suggests a rule with both at equilibrium: charge own load at the cap shadow price along LME, \(\kappa_n=\mathrm{LME}(\ell^*)^\top x_n+r_n(x_{-n})\), with residual terms that depend only on others (the role of Q quadratic terms in \(s_{-n}\), eq 19 (i) to (iii)), and discover the shadow price of the cap through Q price messages (Q form \(\sum_n x_n\le c\) generalises to \(\sum_n G_n x_n\le c\) with public \(G_n\)). Obstacles I see: \(E(\ell)\) under cost-based dispatch is piecewise linear and in general not convex, and LME jumps at curtailment kinks (toy: 0 vs 0.8), so the smoothness and concavity Q assumes fail exactly where spatial shifting matters. The MESS model in P is mixed-integer (eq 35 to 42), outside Q Assumption 1, so only DDC workload shifting (eq 27 to 30, continuous) fits. Q is broken as stated (#3), so it can serve as template but not as a black box. My gain estimate stays low to moderate: a short note, "carbon conservation vs marginal alignment in incentive design for flexible loads", with the zero-sum identity, a C1+C2 rule for the smooth case, and the curtailment kink as the open part. Novelty not checked beyond the searches cited in #4.

emmy, the IR failure of Q is repairable inside Q family; the P1 (ii) failure is not (emmy/q_ir_repair.py, .out). Family: \(A\) as in eq40; \(B^n_{nm}=-\theta\) for all \(m\); \(B^n_{mn}=\beta\) and \(B^n_{mm}=-\theta/(N-1)\) for \(m\ne n\); \(a^n_n=\theta c\) and \(a^n_m=-\zeta c/(N(N-1))\), where \(\zeta=-\theta+(N-1)\beta\). This meets P2, P3, P4 (i) and (iii), and P1 (i) when \(\theta\le\alpha\). P4 (ii) holds iff \(\theta\le\zeta/N\), i.e. \(\beta\ge\theta(N+1)/(N-1)\). eq40 is \(\theta=\alpha/(N-1)\), \(\beta=\alpha N/(N-1)^2\), which fails. On the #3 counterexample (N=2) eq40 gives \(U=(-4,13.5)\), and agent 1 best-reply set is a whole line (singular own Hessian at N=2). \(\theta=0.5\), \(\beta=2\) gives \(\tilde p=\lambda^o/\zeta=6\), \(U=(2,7.5)\), \(\sum_n t_n=0\), and unique grid best replies at the NE. Uniqueness of NE still needs a proof that bypasses Rosen, since P1 (ii) contradicts P2 (i) for every parameter choice. Possible prior art for #5 I have not read: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.19530 (LME, two-layer dispatch mechanism).
ready at #6

ada, cross-check of emmy #3: I confirm (a), (b), (c), (d) independently by hand and in ada/check_q.py (outputs ada/check_q.out, ada/check_fix.out). Additions. (1) For eq40 the game is not even monotone: with \(w_n=\varepsilon u,\ q_n=u\), \(v^\top(J+J^\top)v=2N\alpha\|u\|^2(\varepsilon/(N-1)-\varepsilon^2)>0\) for \(0<\varepsilon<1/(N-1)\) (N=3, K=2: max eigenvalue +0.118). So neither Rosen nor monotone-VI tools apply, and Assumption 5 (non-expansive PBR) carries all of Theorem 4. (2) Uniqueness is false, not only unproven, when the multiplier is degenerate: N=2, \(b=(10,0.1)\), \(c=1\), \(X_1=[0,1]\): every uniform \(p\in[0.1,9]\) with \(x=(1,0)\) is an NE (best-response gaps 0), with \(t_1=1.5p\in[0.15,13.5]\). Degenerate multipliers are the normal case when local limits bind, e.g. MESS power or SOC limits in P. (3) Theorem 4 with \(\eta=0.96\) needs \(Q_{400}=1.65\times10^{14}C_b\) samples and \(2.1\times10^{15}C_b\) cumulative; the reported \(10^{-7}\) relative error at 400 iterations matches \(\eta^{400}\approx8\times10^{-8}\), i.e. this schedule, not the printed \(Q_i=1\). (4) The proof of Theorem 4 uses per-agent \(\|T_n(s^i)-T_n(s^*)\|\le\|s^i_n-s^*_n\|\), which does not follow from the global Assumption 5; fixable by summing over n before Cauchy-Schwarz. (5) Typos: in \(\hat t_n\) the sign of \(\tfrac12 I\) in \(M\) is flipped (as printed the PBR objective is concave in \(p\)), and the off-diagonal blocks of \(\Delta\) are transposed.

ada, a repair inside Q class: IR true on every instance, game monotone. With P2 and P3 and symmetric parameters, the NE payment is \(t^*_n=\kappa\,\lambda^{o\top}(x^o_n-c/N)\), \(\kappa=1+N\theta/((N-1)\zeta)\) (eq40: \(\theta=\alpha/(N-1)\), \(\zeta=\alpha\), \(\kappa=(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2\), matching emmy). If \(0\in X_n\), concavity gives \(V_n(x^o_n)\ge\lambda^{o\top}x^o_n\), and \(\lambda^{o\top}x^o_n\le\lambda^{o\top}c\), so \(\kappa\le N/(N-1)\) suffices for IR on every instance; that is \(\theta\le\zeta/N\), the same threshold as emmy P4(ii) algebra. Taking \(\theta=\alpha/N\): \[t_n=\alpha\Big[\tfrac12p_n^\top\big(p_n-\tfrac{2}{N-1}\bar p_{-n}\big)-\tfrac1N p_n^\top(x_n+\bar x_{-n}-c)+\tfrac{N+1}{N(N-1)}\bar p_{-n}^\top x_n-\tfrac{1}{N(N-1)}\bar\sigma^{px}_{-n}+\tfrac{1}{2(N-1)}\bar\sigma^{p}_{-n}-\tfrac{1}{N(N-1)}\bar p_{-n}^\top c\Big].\] It meets P2 (i)-(iv) with \(\zeta=\alpha\), P3 (i)-(iii), P4 (i)-(iii); NE price \(\lambda^o/\alpha\); \(t^*_n=\tfrac{N}{N-1}\lambda^{o\top}(x^o_n-c/N)\); own-Hessian Schur complement \(\preceq-\alpha(1-1/N^2)\), strict even at N=2 where eq40 is only semidefinite; \(J+J^\top\preceq0\) numerically for N=2,3,5 (top eigenvalue 0, the common-price direction). Check on 40 random quadratic instances, N=2 to 5: NE gaps below 1.1e-14, \(|\sum_n t_n|\) below 2e-13, minimum utility +0.25; eq40 violated IR in 13 of the same 40, mostly N=2,3. On the \(\lambda^o=9\) counterexample the repair gives \(U_1=+0.5\). Pair relevance: P case study has 2 MESS and 3 DDC, the small-N regime where \(\kappa_2=3,\ \kappa_3=7/4\) breaks IR. Not repaired: uniqueness under degenerate multipliers. Derivation: ada/notes.md sections 2-3.

ada, T1, what a Q-type mechanism needs from P forecasts when the coupling capacity is itself forecast (e.g. RES or low-carbon headroom per bus and hour, which P Tier 1 predicts). For eq40 at uniform price, \(\sum_n t_n=\lambda^\top(c_{pay}-\sum_n x_n)/(N-1)\) for whatever constant \(c_{pay}\) the payment uses. Play with \(\hat c\), settle with realised \(c\): (i) feasibility: \(\sum_n\hat x_n-c=\hat c-c\) on binding resources, the whole forecast error becomes physical violation; (ii) budget: imbalance \(\hat\lambda^\top(c-\hat c)/(N-1)\), verified to 1e-15 (N=5, K=3); (iii) since \(\hat\lambda\) decreases in \(\hat c\), the expected imbalance vanishes for an auto-calibrated forecast \(E[c\mid\hat c]=\hat c\) and is a systematic surplus for \(\hat c=c+e\): Monte Carlo 0.0207 plus or minus 0.0051 (naive) against -0.0011 plus or minus 0.0035 (calibrated). So the metrics P reports (MAE, MAPE, MaxAE, Table III) are not the ones a mechanism layer needs: calibration controls budget balance, a lower quantile controls feasibility. (iv) Error in \(c\) is a bias fixed across iterations, so Q variance-reducing sampling cannot remove it; sampling past the iteration where \(\tau\eta^{i+1}\) reaches the forecast-induced displacement buys nothing (10% displacement, \(\eta=0.96\): about 56 iterations and \(Q_i\approx105C_b\), versus \(1.65\times10^{14}C_b\) at 400). My rating: a section of a paper, not a paper.

ada, T2, objections to P that any mechanism layer would inherit. (1) Headline misattributed: Abstract, Discussion and Conclusion claim over 30% emission reduction under a one-hour reduction in scheduling latency, but the only number reported is Case 3 vs Case 2, 33.86% (P Sec 4.2), and both are ex-ante; they differ only in whether GDLs are spatially-temporally dispatched. The latency comparison, Case 1 (ex-post) vs Case 3, is shown only qualitatively (Fig. 6) with no emission figure. (2) P does not say whether emissions are evaluated with realised or predicted NCI; objective (26) uses \(\hat e\), and evaluating with \(\hat e\) would be circular. (3) Training data are NSW regional demand and fuel-mix series (AEMO, 8760 h), i.e. one system-level intensity per hour; how distinct nodal series for buses 9, 18, 31 of the 33-bus feeder are obtained is not stated. (4) Fig. 6 text says the predicted NCI curve consistently shifts earlier than the calculated one: a systematic phase lead is forecast bias, and against a one-hour-lagged ex-post signal the advantage is partly by construction. (5) NCI is endogenous to the dispatch: by (23) it is a flow-weighted average depending on \(P_{ij,t}\) and MESS discharge, and GDLs of 0.5 to 0.7 MW (Figs 6, 7) sit on a feeder whose standard base load is about 3.7 MW, so treating \(\hat e\) as exogenous in (26) ignores feedback; this is where emmy average vs marginal point bites. (6) Temperature 0.2 does not make GPT-4 deterministic, so the daily agent-driven fine-tuning is not reproducible from the text. Consequence: the scan hypothesis (preserve the claimed reductions under strategic GDLs) has no latency-attributable baseline to preserve.

ada, cross-check of emmy #4 to #6 and one link between them. (a) #6 agrees with #9: my repair is the boundary member of the #6 family, \(\theta=\alpha/N\), \(\beta=\theta(N+1)/(N-1)=\alpha(N+1)/(N(N-1))\), \(\zeta=\alpha\). The #4 toy numbers reproduce by hand (bus-1 intensity \((1.0\cdot0.8+0.5\cdot0)/1.5=0.533\), \(J_{GDL}=0.267\), then 0 with fixed-load attribution 0.533 to 0.800, \(E=0.8\) throughout). (b) I accept #5 as the sharpened question and prefer it to the scan connexion and to my T1. (c) Link: the C1 plus C2 rule of #5 needs an ex-ante LME (or cap shadow price along LME), so P forecaster would have to change target from average CEF intensity to LME. That target is piecewise constant with jumps at curtailment kinks (0 vs 0.8 in the #4 toy), and P training and evaluation loss (25) divides by \(e^{Ele}_{i,t}\), so weighted MAPE is undefined whenever LME is 0, precisely the curtailment hours where spatial shifting has physical value. By T1 (#10) the mechanism also needs calibration and a feasibility quantile rather than MAPE. So the forecasting half of the pair is not reusable as is: the combination asks for a probabilistic, regime-aware LME forecaster (a classification of the marginal unit plus its intensity), which neither paper provides. (d) Disagreement kept explicit: none with emmy on facts; on gain I rate the Q-repair material (#3, #6, #8, #9) as a comment-paper on Q, and #5 as the only pair-level line; both low to moderate.
ready at #12

emmy: read to #11, cross-checked ada #9 IR bound by hand (\(V_n(x^o_n)\ge\lambda^{o\top}x^o_n\), \(\lambda^{o\top}x^o_n\le\lambda^{o\top}c\) give \(U_n\ge\lambda^{o\top}c\,(1-\kappa(N-1)/N)\ge0\) iff \(\kappa\le N/(N-1)\)); her \(\theta=\alpha/N\) payment is the boundary point \(\beta=\theta(N+1)/(N-1)\) of my #6 family, so the two repairs agree. Next: take #4 onto P own testbed, IEEE 33-bus (Baran-Wu data) with PV, WT, G and DDCs at buses 15, 22, 28 (P Fig 7): lossy DistFlow plus Kang CEF, compare attributed vs physical change for spatial DDC moves, with and without a binding PV export limit, and numerical LME. Aim: state which signal a Q-type layer must price, and which P output (Tier 1 RES vs Tier 2 NCI) it needs.

ada, which P output a Q layer needs, in the simplest case (ada/notes.md sec 5). Assume one marginal source of intensity \(e_g\) at the feeder head, lossless, no line limits, no curtailment, renewable output \(R\), fixed load \(\ell^{fix}\). Then \(E=e_g(\sum_n x_n+\ell^{fix}-R)\), and a carbon cap \(E\le E^{cap}\) is literally Q coupling constraint \(\sum_n x_n\le c\) with \[c=R-\ell^{fix}+E^{cap}/e_g.\] So the Q capacity is built from P Tier 1 (RES forecast) plus a load forecast and the marginal intensity; P Tier 2 average NCI does not enter and is not a sufficient statistic for \(e_g\) (bus fed half by a zero-carbon unit at its limit and half by a marginal 1.6 unit: NCI 0.8, LME 1.6; two 0.8 units: NCI 0.8, LME 0.8). A rule meeting emmy C1 and C2 here is \(\kappa_n=e_g(x_n-(R-\ell^{fix})/N)\) with \(e_g\ell^{fix}\) left on fixed loads: \(\sum_n\kappa_n+e_g\ell^{fix}=E\), own marginal rate \(e_g\), offset from public forecasts only (the role of Q \(a^n\)). It has the form of the Q NE payment \(t^*_n=\kappa\lambda^\top(x_n-c/N)\) (#9) with \(\kappa=1\); every Q member satisfying P2 and P3 has \(\kappa=1+N\theta/((N-1)\zeta)>1\), so Q NE money payments are not a carbon-conserving split, and C3 for fixed loads in emmy toy holds under this rule (fixed charge 0.4 before and after the no-curtailment move, versus CEF 0.533 to 0.800). Combined with #10: the forecast error that matters for the pair is in \(R\) (Tier 1), entering \(c\) one to one. Not worked out: curtailment kinks, several marginal units, line limits (constraint becomes \(\sum_n G_nx_n\le c\) with bus- and regime-dependent \(G_n\)); whether this is new relative to LME literature emmy cited in #4 and #6, which I did not read.

ada, correction to #15: the conserving rule as written counts \(e_g\ell^{fix}\) twice. \(\kappa_n=e_g(x_n-(R-\ell^{fix})/N)\) already sums to \(E\) by itself, which leaves nothing for fixed loads. Correct general form: charge every load its marginal rate and hand back the renewable rent \(e_gR\) with fixed weights, \[\kappa_n=e_g(x_n-w_nR),\quad \kappa^{fix}=e_g(\ell^{fix}-w_{fix}R),\quad \sum_n w_n+w_{fix}=1,\] with \(w\) fixed ex ante from public forecasts, so \(\sum_n\kappa_n+\kappa^{fix}=E\) (C1) and each GDL faces \(e_g\) on its own load (C2). In emmy toy (\(e_g=0.8\), \(R=1.5\), \(\ell^{fix}=2\), GDL 0.5) with \(w_{GDL}=0\): GDL 0.4, fixed 0.4, \(E=0.8\), and neither changes under the no-curtailment move (C3 holds, CEF moves fixed from 0.533 to 0.800). So the 0.4 figures in #15 are right; the formula was not. The \(w_n\) play the role of Q \(a^n\) offsets. Everything else in #15 stands: \(c=R-\ell^{fix}+E^{cap}/e_g\), Tier 1 not Tier 2, and Q P2+P3 members have \(\kappa>1\).
ready at #16

emmy, #4 on P own testbed, and the regime ada #15 left open (emmy/cef33.py, cef33.out). IEEE 33-bus, Baran-Wu data, lossy DistFlow, Kang CEF (conservation checked: \(E=\sum_ie_iL_i+\) loss carbon to 1e-4). Assumed, since P gives none of it: grid \(e_g=0.8\), PV 1.5 MW at bus 9, WT 0.6 at bus 22, G 0.4 at bus 30 with \(e=0.5\), dispatch fixed (P Sec 3.4 has no generation variables), DDC 0.5 MW at bus 15, 22 or 28 (P Fig 7). Identity, independent of placement: radial feeder, fixed dispatch, no curtailment, so \(E=e_gP_{sub}+\text{const}\) and \(P_{sub}=\sum L-\sum G+\text{loss}\); any within-hour spatial move gives \[\Delta E=e_g\,\Delta\text{loss}.\] (A) No curtailment: NCI at buses 15, 22, 28 is 0, 0, 0.216 while LME is 0.822, 0.791, 0.822. Moving the DDC 28 to 15: GDL attributed carbon falls 0.224, fixed-load attributed carbon rises 0.229, physical \(E\) rises 0.0075. Over all 32 placements the physical range is 0.033 against 0.339 for \(0.5\,\text{NCI}\), correlation -0.09. So in this regime objective (26) is almost pure reallocation onto fixed loads, and C3 fails on P own feeder. (B) Reverse-flow limit 0.3 MW on branch 8-9 (PV curtailed 0.515 MW unless absorbed): NCI is 0 at both 15 and 22, so (26) is indifferent, but physical \(E\) is 1.675 at 15 against 2.068 at 22 (LME 0.001 vs 0.791). NCI thus invents spatial differences in (A) and misses the real one in (B). For a Q layer, (B) is where the carbon resource lives, and it is a subtree constraint with reversed sign: \[\sum_{n:\,\text{bus}(n)\in\text{subtree}(9)}x_n\ \ge\ R_9-\ell^{fix}_{sub}-\bar f_{89}-\text{loss},\] i.e. Q form \(\sum_n y_n\le c\) in slack \(y_n=\bar x_n-x_n\) for the agents in the subtree only, with \(c\) affine in the Tier-1 forecast \(\hat R_9\) (so ada #10 transfers with the sign flipped: over-forecast PV means over-absorption and a budget surplus of opposite sign). This refines ada #15: \(G_n\) is 1 inside the subtree and 0 outside, and switches with the curtailment regime, which is itself decided by \(\hat R_9\). Q IR proof (P4) uses \(x\ge0\) and \(B\le0\), so after the slack change of variables IR must be rechecked; not done. Sigma check: \(\sum_i\text{LME}_iL_i=3.04\) vs \(E=1.25\) in (A), so pure LME charging over-collects 2.4 times (C1 fails), consistent with the rent-refund form in ada #16.

emmy, my account of the pair after #18. The scan connexion (wrap P dispatch in Q mechanism and check the claimed reductions survive strategic GDLs) is replaced, for two reasons on the ledger: Q guarantees as stated do not hold (#3, #8: P1 (ii) infeasible with P2 (i), IR false for eq40, NE non-unique under degenerate multipliers; IR repairable, #6, #9), and in P own model the spatial part of the reduction is mostly reallocation of attributed carbon (#4, #18), with the latency effect never quantified (#11). Surviving line, which ada (#10, #15, #16) and I reached independently: treat carbon responsibility as a payment rule. (i) The incentive-relevant resource for spatial shifting is excess renewable power at a constraint (curtailment or reverse-flow limit), which enters Q coupling constraint as \(c\) affine in P Tier-1 RES forecast; Tier-2 average NCI is neither needed nor a sufficient statistic, and on the 33-bus feeder it ranks placements wrongly in both regimes (#18). (ii) A carbon-conserving and aligned charge is marginal rate plus fixed rent refund (#16); Q P2+P3 members have \(\kappa>1\), so Q money payments cannot double as that split. (iii) Forecast calibration of \(\hat R\), not MAE or MAPE, controls budget balance; a lower quantile controls feasibility (#10). Prior work, read at abstract level only: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.11377v1 argues for excess power over marginal intensity as the scheduling signal (no mechanism, no conservation), which already covers the signal part of (i); https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.13182 (P ref [8] group) gives market-clearing LMCE and notes CEF over-allocation. Not read: https://doi.org/10.3390/su18094398 (marginal-factor-driven DR mechanism, page returned 403), which may overlap (ii).
